title: VIP Q&A with Vishen
overview: In this smaller VIP session Jason Goldberg relays upvoted questions while Vishen, joining from London, answers on beginners and pre-revenue businesses, organic high-ticket sales, the internal shift behind authority, overwhelm, signature methods, pricing signals, website structure and whether authority can be guaranteed. You also see him use his own AI companion live to prioritise questions, digest a lesson he never watched, and run a funnel analysis on an attendee's website.
key_ideas: You can be pre-revenue, but not pre-direction. The programme and the method work for a founder who is not yet earning as an authority or for an employee who is brilliant at something, as long as you know roughly what you want to be known for; if you are still choosing between longevity and meditation, find your niche first.

High-ticket coaching can be sold entirely organically if the customer spends real time with you. Instagram grabs attention but shows only snippets; the bond is built in long-form YouTube (30 minutes to two hours, possibly across several videos), and from there you go straight to the high-end offer, as Daniel Priestley and Jay Shetty do.

The internal shift behind authority is your rate of learning: how fast you absorb, connect disparate ideas ('idea collision') and act. Vishen's model of the future is three brains working together: your human mind, an AI brain that maps your knowledge, and an AI companion that studies, listens and drafts for you.

Overwhelm is not too many options; it is unstructured chaos plus a tight timeline. Work moves through three levels (understanding, optimisation, automation): understand the principle, build a trained AI project that improves with each correction until you do the work of ten people, then let automation run the business so work becomes optional.

Package and name your signature method before building the low-ticket rung. The method feeds ideas, feedback and content for every other product, and you often underestimate it: the six-phase meditation began as an addendum to a book before an R&B star and an NBA player found it on YouTube.

Inspiration hedges its bets. Vishen reads from Elizabeth Gilbert's Big Magic on 'multiple discovery': the same idea whispers to several people, and the one who acts is the one the universe resources, so the seed of a method you are sitting on should be put out into the world, even free, to see what people say.

Understand your market through open-ended questions, not spreadsheets. Ask people to hit record and speak for five or ten minutes, feed the answers to AI, and turn the analysis into an 'agent guide' that every AI you use reads so your slides, emails and offers respect where your audience actually is.

On your website, the signature offer sits below a free or low-priced invitation (a masterclass, a quiz, a sample). 'Low' is relative to the market: $99 is cheap for a business tool and expensive for a parenting course. Mindvalley's meditation site uses a quiz that leads to seven free days and then a subscription.

AI organises thought; it does not replace the coach. A good coach is presence, felt energy and intuitive response, none of which the AI has. Vishen describes himself as an intuition trainer who happens to be a computer scientist, and refusing AI in business today is like refusing laptops.

Authority cannot be guaranteed for one specific topic, because your first bet may not hold your interest (Vishen lost interest in being a webinar authority). What can be guaranteed is that once you learn the method you can point it at manifesting, meditation, AI or whatever comes next.

frameworks.name: Three levels of work
steps: Understanding: learn the principle (for example Cialdini's levels of influence, basic copywriting) without trying to become the master yourself
Optimisation: build a trained AI project that becomes the master, correct its first rough outputs, and let it learn your voice until you do the work of ten people
Automation: the AI monitors your goals, calendar, inbox and numbers and keeps you focused, so overwhelm disappears and work becomes optional

frameworks.name: Three brains for accelerated learning
steps: Your human mind, which supplies the stories, personality, presence and heart
An AI brain: a map of your notes, ideas and knowledge that can be searched for idea collisions
An AI companion with its own personality that listens to meetings, studies lessons for you, understands your learning gaps and drafts outputs like a chief of staff

frameworks.name: Organic path to high-ticket sales
steps: Long-form YouTube videos (or a podcast) where the customer spends 30 minutes to two hours with you, sometimes across five to seven videos
Direct invitation from the long-form content to the high-end coaching or programme

frameworks.name: Open-ended market research with AI
steps: Build a simple quiz with a few factual questions (location, income) and one open-ended question
Ask people to click record and speak for five to ten minutes rather than type
Feed the responses to AI and ask it to analyse the audience's emotional state, frustrations and blocks
Turn the analysis into an agent guide that every AI project you run reads before producing anything

frameworks.name: Website layering
steps: Top of page: a free or low-priced entry point such as 'watch my masterclass', 'take the quiz' or a sample
Below it: the signature offer for people who are ready
Price the entry point relative to your market, and let the free taste lead directly into the paid product

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: A good coach is more than just articulation. A good coach is presence.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: All the AI is doing is organizing bulk information to increase your intelligence.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: But overwhelm is not so much multitude of options. It's unstructured chaos in your brain and a tight timeline.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: So sometimes, we often don't see how powerful something so simple that we've figured out can be to someone else.

quotes.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
quotes.text: Once you learn the method, you can point it. It's like a weapon you can point, a beautiful, gracious, conscious weapon you can point in many different directions.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: The most upvoted question, from Dinesh, Deepti, Sarah and others: is this for me if I'm a beginner, pre-revenue, just starting?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Yes, as long as you know directionally what you want to be known for. You might be a founder already earning from your company but pre-revenue as an authority, or an employee who is brilliant at something and wants to start teaching it. If you still don't know whether you want to do longevity or meditation, find your niche first, because otherwise you'll be stuck.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Zoe, Rachel and Katherine ask: can you grow a high-ticket coaching programme with only organic marketing? I can't afford ads.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Absolutely. Become known for your thing on YouTube or Instagram, but remember Instagram only grabs attention; the customer needs to spend 30 minutes to two hours with you in long-form YouTube before they buy high-end. Daniel Priestley and Jay Shetty both do this, and it's all organic.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Annalisa asks: beyond automation and audience growth, what internal or identity shift do you need to make to step into your own authority and positioning?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: The shift is your rate of learning: how rapidly you learn, connect ideas and bring two disparate ideas together, which we call idea collision. We teach a new way of learning where you have your human mind, an AI brain and an AI companion that studies for you, and I'll show you how mine digested a four-hour Daniel Priestley lesson I never watched and turned it into a plan my team is now running.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Someone in the chat says this would kill human coaching.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: No. The AI doesn't have your stories, your personality, your eye contact, your vibe or your energy. A good coach is presence, felt energy and intuitive response; all the AI is doing is organising thought. Notice how quickly it found the most important question tonight, but the response came from my heart.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Darren asks how we make sure we're not over-committing ourselves to multiple products and services.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: I teach three levels of work: understanding, optimisation and automation. Understand the principle, then build an AI project that becomes the master and improves with every correction until you do the work of ten people; then decide whether to do ten people's work or stop working Fridays. Overwhelm isn't too many options, it's unstructured chaos and a tight timeline, so remove the timeline first.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Sylvie has decades of expertise and a strong network, doesn't want a massive company or to be a full-time content creator, and creates transformational leadership experiences. What's the minimum viable ecosystem to expand her reach without diluting human connection?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: I don't want to answer without understanding her business, so I'll feed her website into an AI project trained on funnel design across the top expert businesses and we'll come back to it. Ideally you use AI to analyse and map everything and also have the one-on-one conversation; the analysis came back proposing a specific funnel model and a set of questions Sylvie should answer in her own AI, which we'll send her.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Does it work for B2B or only B2C?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: The same process works for B2B. Sometimes the platform shifts, for example more LinkedIn than Instagram, but the same principles of building a funnel and a business apply.

dialogue.speaker: Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)
dialogue.text: Joan Francisco asks several times: are missed sessions recorded?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Yes, all sessions are recorded and you get them, along with detailed student notes in the classroom. You can also ask the AI companion how to apply a lesson to your own company given everything it knows about you, and it will do that even if you never read the notes.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Miles already has an audience, a monthly live event, an email list and a high-touch practice combining nervous-system, somatic and parts work. Should he name and package the signature method first, or build the low-ticket rung and let it reveal the method?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Package the signature method first; it gives you the ideas, feedback and content to build every other rung. My six-phase meditation was only an addendum in my book until I put a video on YouTube and Miguel and Reggie Jackson found it, and it became a national bestseller. Get it out, even free, and see what people say. As Elizabeth Gilbert writes, inspiration whispers to many people and supports the one who acts.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Dr Wala Mohamed asks: at what point should I raise my prices, and what signals (demand, conversion, testimonials, wait lists) tell me my audience is ready without damaging trust?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: Use pattern recognition rather than spreadsheets. Ask your audience an open-ended question, ideally have them click record and speak for five or ten minutes, feed it into AI and let it analyse where they are; that analysis becomes an agent guide every AI you use reads. Your AIs will then understand your market better than any human, and that understanding tells you what they're ready for.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Dianne asks: given the product ladder you shared, what should be on my website: the signature offer, the low ticket, or what?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: The signature offer, with an invitation above it to something free or low-priced for people not yet ready: watch my masterclass, take the quiz, buy a sample. Low is relative to your market. On our meditation site a free quiz recommends seven meditations, you get the app free for seven days, and then it becomes a paid subscription; the free taste leads directly to paying.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Dr Ezequiel Newbery says he's already making $100K a year. Is Mastery useful for him? He wants to scale and make full use of AI.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: If you're making over $100K as an author there's a level beyond Mastery called the Guild, modelled on medieval guilds where craftsmen shared best practices. It's 90 people by application, many of them Mindvalley authors; each commits to sharing one key insight a month in the group, I teach one advanced lesson a month, and everyone signs an NDA. That's where you're in the same room with Marisa Peer, Regan Hillyer and me.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Dawn Grant had a $270-a-month course bringing in $10,000 a month from a free web class and word of mouth. She switched to a $5,000 lifetime price, sold $25,000 in three months and nothing since, then tried tiers and a subscription with minimal sales. Any advice?

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: It's tricky and I need to see the business and the campaign before diagnosing, because it could be a lot of things. I've put her website and question into my AI; it has come back with a pricing analysis that's too complex, so I'll have it explain it simply and we'll share it tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Andrea asks whether becoming an authority is guaranteed if we follow the teachings. It seems everyone else got big because Vishen hand-selected them.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: I do spot potential, but selecting someone isn't what made them big; I had to put them through a process. Bert Goldman's Quantum Jumping started as a lunch conversation about a little book, and the method turned it into a million-dollar launch. I can't guarantee authority in one specific thing, because you may lose interest, but I can guarantee that once you learn the method you can apply it to many different fields.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Someone in the chat asks which level of Claude subscription they need.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: There are so many options that you should ask Claude itself: describe how you're using it and ask what level you'd need. AI is very honest about that.

dialogue.speaker: Jason Goldberg
dialogue.text: Some attendees are saying they don't like AI.

dialogue.speaker: Vishen Lakhiani
dialogue.text: AI is just the accelerator; it's like saying you want to be an expert but you don't like laptops. You can use pen and paper, and I respect that, but I can't teach business today without teaching the latest tools. I'm an intuition trainer who happens to be a computer scientist, so you get both.

next_steps: Write your niche in one line, even if it is vague, and confirm you are pre-revenue rather than pre-direction.
Name your signature method and publish one piece of content teaching it, free, to see what people say.
Add one open-ended, voice-recorded question to your next audience survey and feed the answers into an AI to build a short audience brief.
Rearrange your homepage so a free or low-priced entry point (masterclass, quiz or sample) sits above your signature offer.
attribution_notes: Lines are labelled 'Vishen' and 'Mindvalley' (Jason Goldberg reading upvoted questions), so attribution is high confidence. Vishen introduced the first two questions himself after having his AI rank them, and later answered two chat comments (B2B and recordings) without Jason, so those are marked 'Audience question (read by Vishen Lakhiani)' and the chat comments are attributed to Jason as relayed remarks. A few audio dropouts left Jason re-reading the Miles and Sylvie questions; the price-clarification question was omitted as administrative. Names corrected: Marissa Pierre = Marisa Peer, Reagan = Regan Hillyer, Daniel Prisley = Daniel Priestley, Jay Chetty = Jay Shetty.
